title: Cascade throttle and customer communication for mixed-deployment regressions
creator: Anika Patel
description: During a staggered model rollout across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments we observed a correlated degradation pattern: elevated rejection rates and hallucination spikes in canary cohorts tied to a new attention-kernel selection heuristic. This ticket coordinates an operational mitigation (staged throttle + pin), customer liaison steps, and the follow-up engineering fixes required to resolve the regression and restore SLOs.
reproduction_steps:
1) Deploy model v4.7-beta to a small canary fleet in hosted/dedicated environments using ramp config 'rampX'.
2) Run the synthetic prompt suite (prompt-set 'synth-qa-2026-02') at 50rps per node.
3) Observe increased token rejection errors (ERR_TOKEN_DROP) and response divergence against golden outputs after 800 tokens.
4) Reproduce locally using runtime image 'redwood/runtime:1.20-rc3' with kernel flag '--kernel-selection=adaptive'.
mitigation_plan: Short term: immediate staged throttle (reduce canary ingress by 70%) and application of a model pin to last known-good variant for affected tenants. Mid term: revert adaptive kernel selection on canary cohorts and enable KV-cache-compatibility patch referenced in PR. Long term: add a runtime guard that disallows kernel selection changes while KV-cache warmup is in progress and extend canary observability for hallucination metrics.
communications: 2026-02-20 11:05 - Support: initial inbound from large customer (AcmeHealth) reporting semantic regressions in private deployment - flagged as P0
2026-02-20 12:30 - Oncall notes: throttled new ramp for hosted canary to 30% and opened ENG-57129

2026-02-21 09:00 - Customer liaison (SRE-Sales): outbound to impacted customers describing temporary pin and expected timeline: 'We have pinned your model to v4.6.2 and throttled new rollouts; ETA for full resolution 72 hours.'
2026-02-22 16:40 - Customer update: committed to weekly postmortem and offered a sandbox for validation of the fix.
decisions: 1) We will prefer a staged throttle + pin over a global rollback to minimize blast radius for Dedicated customers that require capacity guarantees.
2) Reverting adaptive kernel selection on canary fleets rather than a model rollback — trade-off: temporary loss of a small latency improvement vs. immediate quality recovery.

3) For Private deployments, changes will be pushed as a non-disruptive configuration flag to respect customer change control; we will not auto-revert on tenant-managed clusters without explicit consent.

notes: - Initial root cause signal correlates kernel-selection 'adaptive' with stale KV cache warmup on long-context sessions (>800 tokens).
- Edge case found: some Private deployments with customized quantization profiles triggered a fallback path that bypassed KV reconciliation.
- Legal/compliance flagged that customer-facing notes for Private deployments must pass security review before posting; we have queued a short copy review with Security (ticket SEC-2026-011).
